text:
Kevin L.: Hey team — putting up a request to reserve GPU capacity in eu-central for Q3 traffic growth. Proposal: 12-month committed capacity equivalent to 8x A100 (or compatible instances). Estimated commit cost: $1,120,000 over 12 months (~35% vs current on-demand). Need sign-off to submit procurement request and start the CSP negotiation. cc @Priya S. @Maria G.
Maria G.: Can you attach a short breakdown (unit cost, hours, utilization assumptions)? Also: what SLA/availability guarantee do we get with the reservation?
Kevin L.: Quick numbers below, happy to expand. Assumptions: 8 units * 24h * 365 * utilization 0.78 => committed utilization ~6.24 units avg. On-demand today we're at ~5.1 avg with spikes.
```
Unit monthly (reserved) per-unit: $9,333
12-mo commit total: $1,120,000
On-demand baseline (12-mo est): $1,720,000
Estimated annual savings: ~$600k (~35%)
Expected utilization: 78% (conservative)
```
Jon P.: Can we instead do a mixed approach: 6 reserved + 2 ondemand for peak? That reduces commit and keeps headroom. Latency to EU customers might still be fine if we burst from nearby region for short tail.
Maria G.: We prefer local reserved for the majority to hit p95 latency targets. But Jon's idea makes sense to reduce capex risk. How much does 6 vs 8 change the price?
Kevin L.: 6-unit 12-mo commit would be ~$840k (same per-unit pricing). Savings vs on-demand ~51% on the committed portion, overall ~28% because more ondemand. Tradeoff: less guaranteed capacity during sustained high traffic.
Priya S.: From finance: we need a short ROI doc and an exec approval if >$500k commit for 12mo. Please include spend bucketing (hosted vs dedicated vs reserved), expected break-even, and contingency if utilization drops below 60%. Also we should slot this into the cloud spend forecast for Q3.
infra-bot: Billing alert: eu-central GPU on-demand spend +42% MoM, peak at 03:20 UTC yesterday.
Kevin L.: Noted. My proposal: start with 6-unit 12-mo commit ($840k) + 2-unit monthly flex for peak. That keeps commit under the exec sign-off threshold for now, and we still get capacity guarantees. I'll prepare the ROI and a risk mitigation plan (right-sizing + opt-out window) and link procurement PR.
Maria G.: Sounds reasonable. Please include a canary rollout plan for new nodes (Jon, can you draft?). Also add a network egress/cross-region cost estimate — moving KV-cache snapshots across regions can add nontrivial cost.
Jon P.: Will draft canary + autoscaling rules. Plan: bring 2 reserved into production first week, run traffic cutover 10% -> 50% -> 100% across two weeks, monitor latency/cost metrics.
Priya S.: For initial approval, finance can greenlight procurement request up to $300k pending the ROI doc and a 30-min review. Anything above requires C-level sign-off. Please schedule the review for tomorrow 10:00 CET.
Kevin L.: Thanks — I'll update the PR and post the ROI doc before the review. Link to PR: https://redwood.internal/prs/4821 (will update with numbers).
Maria G.: Great. After procurement kick-off, we should also open a CloudOps ticket to reserve IP ranges and update firewall rules.
Jon P.: Noted. I'll create the deployment runbook and the CloudOps ticket. :thumbsup:
Priya S.: Thanks everyone. If we see utilization hold >85% for 2 months we should revisit and consider expanding the commit.
Kevin L.: Agreed. I'll capture that as an automatic review trigger in the procurement notes. :eyes:
